title.narrative: Activity under preparation CAT - Central Asia Global Talent Gateway

description.narrative: Central Asia faces persistent challenges in developing a skilled workforce. Despite reforms, Vocational Education and Training (VET) struggles to attract learners and fails to equip graduates with market-relevant skills. This undermines economic growth, limits sectoral development, and creates barriers for local and foreign businesses (World Bank, 2019).[1]. As Global Gateway investments expand across the region, targeted skills development must prioritize aligning workforce capabilities with emerging labour market demands to support EU projects and ensure sustainable business growth.The action will establish a EUR 5 million regional pilot facility covering Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. It will help Central Asian countries and their education systems prepare local people for jobs linked to Global Gateway investments and related value chains by translating investment and sector demand into practical, recognised and country-anchored skills responses. The action will build on a number of achievements of the ongoing regional programme ¿Dialogue for Active and Resourceful Youth in Central Asia¿ (DARYA, 2022¿2027, EUR 10 million) implemented by the European Training Foundation (ETF), notably the occupational profiles developed in Global Gateway sectors, the high-level working group of employment and education ministries from the five Central Asian countries, the regional mapping of skills providers (which is in the making), and work on labour-market intelligence and qualifications.The programme will draw on DARYA¿s lessons and tools but will not be a phase II; while continuing the engagement with Central Asian governments, it will broaden participation to EU Member States, EFIs and EU and local private sector actors, and place a stronger focus on skills linked to employment opportunities in Global Gateway priority areas through concrete, business-oriented and hands-on activities.This pilot project, will be demand/opportunity driven and composed of short, modular, market¿relevant training and certification offers and targeted country¿sector pilots to test scalable models. It will also strengthen selected TVET centres. To respond to the limited envelope, the action combines regional tools and methods with a limited number of practical pilots in selected countries and sectors. Regional tools may include methods and templates for investment-linked skills analysis, occupational profiling, competence clusters, provider-readiness assessment, modular training, micro-credentials, recognition of prior learning, work-based learning and certification pathways. Practical pilots will be selected in line with existing and future Global Gateway priorities where investment demand, employer/operator commitment and provider feasibility are demonstrated.The activity portfolio is framed around the key thematic area of Trans¿Caspian Transport Corridor. A focus on TCTC/transport-logistics offers a visible regional entry point across most Central Asian countries and can be linked to practical skills needs in transport planning, infrastructure maintenance, logistics, supply chains, road, railway and maritime services.
